concept.name: Full-Text Inverted Indexes

relationships.description: Connects Full-Text Inverted Indexes to database indexing in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: A term-to-document mapping backed by compressed sorted postings lists, FST term dictionaries, and immutable LSM-style segments that powers sub-50ms full-text search and BM25 ranking.
spark.keyTakeaway: Inverted indexes turn O(N) document scans into O(k) compressed posting-list intersections using FST dictionaries, delta+bitpacking, and Block-Max WAND pruning.

concept.whyItMatters: Scanning millions of JSON documents or logs with `LIKE '%term%'` forces O(N) disk and CPU reads. An inverted index—used by Apache Lucene, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and PostgreSQL GIN—pre-tokenizes text into normalized terms and stores sorted, compressed lists of matching document IDs, enabling sub-50ms boolean, phrase, and BM25-ranked queries at petabyte scale.
whenToUse: You need fast keyword, phrase, prefix, or BM25 relevance-ranked search across unstructured text fields in millions or billions of documents.
Queries combine multiple filter predicates (`status:200 AND region:us-east`) where intersecting compressed roaring bitmaps or postings lists beats B-tree composite indexes.
You can tolerate near-real-time (NRT) visibility delays (typically 1 second in Lucene/Elasticsearch) in exchange for high write throughput via immutable segments.
whenNotToUse: Your workload requires strict ACID point-updates on individual fields at high frequency—updating 1 field in an immutable Lucene segment marks the old doc tombstoned and re-indexes the entire document.
You primarily run numeric range aggregations or time-series scans (`timestamp > T`), where columnar engines (ClickHouse, Parquet) or BKD trees outperform inverted postings.
Your search requires purely semantic similarity across synonyms with zero lexical overlap—use dense vector HNSW indexes (or combine both in hybrid search).
keyPoints: Text ingestion runs through an analyzer pipeline (character filters -> tokenizer -> token filters like lowercase/stemming) to emit normalized terms; index and query analyzers must match.
A Finite State Transducer (FST) in Lucene maps term prefixes in memory to disk offsets in the term dictionary (`.tim`/`.tip`), keeping only ~1–5% of dictionary metadata in RAM.
Postings lists store sorted `docID`s as delta gaps (`d_i - d_{i-1}`) packed via Frame-of-Reference (FOR / SIMD-BP128) or Roaring Bitmaps, shrinking 32-bit docIDs to ~2–6 bits each.
Phrase queries (`"distributed lock"`) require storing positional offsets inside postings, which typically doubles or triples index disk size.

To avoid mutating compressed postings in place, engines write immutable segments (LSM pattern) and merge them asynchronously in the background (`TieredMergePolicy`), filtering deleted docs via a live-docs bitset.

examples.title: Elasticsearch / Lucene E-Commerce Catalog Search
examples.scenario: A 50-million-SKU catalog handles 15,000 QPS for multi-word queries (`"wireless noise cancelling headphones"`) with brand filters and BM25 relevance ranking (`k1=1.2, b=0.75`).
examples.outcome: Lucene's FST resolves each term in O(term_length), skips non-matching blocks via Block-Max WAND pruning without scoring all 50M docs, and returns top-20 results in <25 ms p99.

examples.title: PostgreSQL GIN Index on JSONB & `tsvector` Logs
examples.scenario: An audit log table with 80M rows stores `tsvector` message bodies and JSONB tags, experiencing 2,000 inserts/sec alongside ad-hoc keyword lookups.
examples.outcome: Enabling `GIN` with `fastupdate = on` buffers incoming postings in a pending list before batch-merging into the B-tree of posting lists, keeping inserts fast while serving keyword queries in <15 ms.

tradeOffs.pro: Immutable sorted segments compress postings tightly and allow zero-lock OS page-cache reads.
tradeOffs.con: Background segment merging consumes significant disk I/O and CPU, and document updates require tombstone + full re-index.

tradeOffs.factor: Positional & N-Gram Indexing vs. Disk Footprint
tradeOffs.pro: Storing positions and edge-ngrams enables exact phrase matching and instant autocomplete.
tradeOffs.con: Increases index size by 2x–5x and slows down ingestion throughput.

tradeOffs.factor: NRT Refresh Interval vs. Segment Count
tradeOffs.pro: Short refresh intervals (e.g., 1s) make newly indexed documents searchable almost immediately.
tradeOffs.con: Sub-second refreshes create hundreds of tiny segments, exhausting file descriptors and stalling merges.

failureModes.name: Segment Explosion from Aggressive Refresh
failureModes.description: Calling explicit `_refresh` on every write or setting `refresh_interval: 100ms` generates thousands of tiny segments, causing `Too many open files` (`EMFILE`) and merge-throttling stalls.
failureModes.mitigation: Keep `refresh_interval` at `1s` (or `30s` during bulk backfills) and never invoke `_refresh` per request in production write paths.

failureModes.name: High-Frequency Term Scanning (Stopword / Skew)
failureModes.description: Queries containing ubiquitous terms (`"the"`, `"error"`, `"2026"`) match 80% of documents, forcing full posting-list decompression unless pruned.
failureModes.mitigation: Use Block-Max WAND (enabled by default in Lucene 8+) for top-K BM25 pruning, or index high-frequency boilerplate with `common_terms` / stopword filtering.

failureModes.name: Index-Time vs. Query-Time Analyzer Mismatch
failureModes.description: Indexing text with a Porter stemmer (`"running" -> "run"`) while querying with a `keyword` or unstemmed analyzer returns zero matches.
failureModes.mitigation: Explicitly bind identical analyzer pipelines for index and search unless intentionally using asymmetric `edge_ngram` (index) + `standard` (search) patterns.

failureModes.name: Deep Pagination Heap Exhaustion
failureModes.description: Requesting `from=50000, size=20` across 10 shards forces every shard to score and return 50,020 docIDs to the coordinator for an O(N log K) merge sort.
failureModes.mitigation: Use `search_after` with a Point-in-Time (PIT) cursor and tie-breaker `_shard_doc` sort instead of deep `from`/`size` offsets.

commonMistakes: Storing large unsearched JSON blobs inside `_source` or indexing every field with `positions` when only `keyword` exact match is needed.
Allowing PostgreSQL GIN `gin_pending_list_limit` (default 4 MB) to bloat or flush synchronously on a random user insert, causing p99 write spikes.
Running wildcard queries with a leading `*` (`*error*`), which defeats the FST prefix dictionary and forces a full scan of every term in the index.
Leaving shard counts oversized (e.g., 50 shards for 5 GB of data), which multiplies per-query FST/BM25 overhead by 50x.
Evaluating BM25 IDF per-shard on small datasets (`dfs_query_then_fetch` disabled), skewing relevance scores when term frequencies vary across shards.

sections.content:
## The idea

A forward index maps `docID -> [terms]`, which answers "what is in document 42?" in O(1) but forces an O(N) scan to find all documents containing `"raft"`. An **inverted index** transposes that relationship into `term -> sorted [docID_1, docID_2, ...]`.

Modern engines like Apache Lucene split this into two tiers: an in-memory **Finite State Transducer (FST)** that maps term prefixes to disk offsets in constant time per character, and on-disk **compressed postings lists** grouped in 128-doc blocks. Because `docID`s are strictly increasing, storing deltas (`doc_i - doc_{i-1}`) reduces 32-bit integers to tiny values that pack into 2–6 bits per document via SIMD bitpacking.

## Concrete walkthrough

Suppose we index three documents for query `"raft consensus"`:
- `Doc 10`: `"raft leader election"`
- `Doc 12`: `"paxos and raft consensus"`
- `Doc 19`: `"raft consensus protocol"`

1. **Tokenize & invert**: Term `"raft"` maps to `[10, 12, 19]`; `"consensus"` maps to `[12, 19]`.
2. **Delta encode**: `"raft"` stores `[10, +2, +7]` (with `tf` `[1, 1, 1]` and positions `[0]`, `[2]`, `[0]`). `"consensus"` stores `[12, +7]` (positions `[3]`, `[1]`).
3. **Query execution**: Galloping skip-list intersection aligns `"raft"` (`10 -> 12`) with `"consensus"` (`12`), finds `Doc 12` (`pos 2` followed by `pos 3` -> phrase match!) and `Doc 19` (`pos 0` followed by `pos 1` -> phrase match!), then scores both using BM25.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / BM25 scoring and Block-Max WAND pruning
sections.content:
## BM25 scoring and Block-Max WAND pruning

Boolean matching alone treats a 10,000-word article mentioning `"redis"` once the same as a 50-word note repeating it 5 times. **BM25** fixes this with diminishing term-frequency saturation (`k1 ≈ 1.2`), document-length normalization (`b ≈ 0.75` against average doc length), and Inverse Document Frequency (`IDF`) so rare terms dominate.

For top-K queries, **Block-Max WAND** stores the maximum possible BM25 contribution for every 128-doc block in skip metadata. If the sum of remaining block upper bounds cannot beat the current K-th best score in the priority queue, the engine skips decompressing the entire 128-doc block—cutting CPU work by 5–10x on multi-term OR queries.

## Index engine comparison

| Feature | Apache Lucene / Elasticsearch | PostgreSQL `GIN` | Relational B-Tree (`LIKE 'foo%'`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Storage Layout** | Immutable LSM segments + FST | Mutable B-tree of posting trees/lists | Single B-tree on full column |
| **Compression** | Delta + SIMD-BP128 (~2–6 bits/doc) | Varbyte / Roaring-like posting compression | Prefix compression only |
| **Relevance Ranking** | Native BM25 + Block-Max WAND | `ts_rank` (no Block-Max pruning) | None |
| **ACID Point Updates** | Tombstone + full doc re-index (NRT) | Full MVCC ACID (`fastupdate` buffer) | Full MVCC ACID |
| **Phrase / Proximity** | Native via `.pos` stream | Supported via `tsvector` positions | Unsupported |

## Failure modes

- **Sub-second refresh thrashing**: Frequent refreshes spawn thousands of tiny unmerged segments, inflating heap FST overhead and exhausting OS file descriptors.
- **Wildcard prefix scans**: Leading wildcards (`*timeout`) bypass the FST prefix structure and enumerate every term in the segment.
- **Analyzer drift**: Changing stemming or synonym rules in a search template without reindexing silently drops recall.
- **Deep `from` pagination**: Fetching page 5,000 across 10 shards materializes 500,000 sorted hits in coordinator heap instead of using `search_after` cursors.

## LSM segment lifecycle and deletions

Because postings lists are delta-encoded and bit-packed, deleting or updating a document in place would require rewriting entire megabyte blocks. Instead, Lucene maintains a tiny **live-docs bitset** (1 bit per doc in the segment). Deleting a document simply flips its bit to `0` in RAM/disk.

Background **TieredMergePolicy** threads periodically merge multiple small segments into larger ones, physically purging tombstoned documents and reclaiming space. During bulk data loads, setting `refresh_interval = -1` and `number_of_replicas = 0` temporarily suspends segment creation and replication overhead, boosting indexing throughput by 3–5x.

## Practical checklist

- Match index-time and query-time analyzers explicitly; disable `positions` (`index_options: docs`) on fields that never need phrase queries.
- Keep `refresh_interval >= 1s` (`30s` for log pipelines) and never call `_refresh` on every write.
- Use `keyword` / Roaring-bitmap filter contexts (`filter` clause) instead of `must` so non-scoring predicates bypass BM25.
- Replace deep `from/size` pagination with `search_after` + Point-in-Time (PIT) tokens.
- Target 10–50 GB per shard in Elasticsearch/OpenSearch to balance FST heap overhead against parallel query fan-out.

simulation.title: Interactive Simulation: Full Text Inverted Indexes

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: A term-to-document mapping backed by compressed sorted postings lists, FST term dictionaries, and immutable LSM-style segments that powers sub-50ms full-text search and BM25 ranking.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Compressed Postings applies the primary invariant and coordinates with WAND & BM25 Scorer.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, WAND & BM25 Scorer experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Keep `refresh_interval` at `1s` (or `30s` during bulk backfills) and never invoke `_refresh` per request in production write paths.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Inverted indexes turn O(N) document scans into O(k) compressed posting-list intersections using FST dictionaries, delta+bitpacking, and Block-Max WAND pruning.
Avoid trap: Storing large unsearched JSON blobs inside `_source` or indexing every field with `positions` when only `keyword` exact match is needed.
Avoid trap: Allowing PostgreSQL GIN `gin_pending_list_limit` (default 4 MB) to bloat or flush synchronously on a random user insert, causing p99 write spikes.
When to reach for it: You need fast keyword, phrase, prefix, or BM25 relevance-ranked search across unstructured text fields in millions or billions of documents.
When to reach for it: Queries combine multiple filter predicates (`status:200 AND region:us-east`) where intersecting compressed roaring bitmaps or postings lists beats B-tree composite indexes.

putItTogether.title: Putting Full Text Inverted Indexes Together
putItTogether.summary: Inverted indexes turn O(N) document scans into O(k) compressed posting-list intersections using FST dictionaries, delta+bitpacking, and Block-Max WAND pruning.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Full Text Inverted Indexes before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Lucene's FST resolves each term in O(term_length), skips non-matching blocks via Block-Max WAND pruning without scoring all 50M docs, and returns top-20 results in <25 ms p99.
